iti62:2.1: This set is found at [dn33:1.10.111]() and [sn48.23:1.3](), but the exact meaning is not obvious. The verses here offer our best clues, so I annotate them closely. They went on to become a standard Abhidhamma set, found at [vb5:24.1](); the explanation there is minimal, but seems to agree with the later commentary. So do the explanations at [ps1.4:89.2](), [ne37:392.2]() [ne5:28.1]() and The set is indicative of a growing fascination with analyzing the details of what exactly happens in the process of enlightenment.
iti62:2.3: The key term is _aññā_ (“enlightenment”), which is used throughout the Suttas to indicate the realization of arahantship specifically. For this reason I am not convinced by the commentarial explanation, which takes it as the knowledge arising first in a stream-enterer. | “The faculty of understanding that one’s enlightenment is imminent” is literally, “The faculty aware that ‘I shall know the unknown’”.
iti62:2.6: Now follow three verses, which seem to correlate one-by-one to the three faculties, and constitute the earliest explanation of the three faculties. In brief, I think the three faculties apply to: (1) the one on the path to arahantship; (2) one on the occasion of realizing arahantship; (3) one living as an arahant.
iti62:3.1: This first line indicates that the first faculty is restricted to those who have entered the noble path. The commentary takes this as meaning *all* those who have entered the noble path, but I think it is a subset.
iti62:3.3: In the Suttas, this is normally the “knowledge of the ending of defilements”, which is characteristic of the arahant (eg. [sn12.23]()).
iti62:3.4: Ending of defilements “without delay” (_anantarā_) is taught numerous time as the advanced meditation practice aimed squarely at arahantship in this very life, typically explained as seeing the impermanence of the five aggregates ([sn22.55:10.1](), [sn22.81:5.1](), [an5.170](), [an6.27](), [an6.28]()). Also similar is the stock phrase “enlightenment in this very life” (_diṭṭheva dhamme aññā_, [sn47.36:1.9]()). This seems to exclude most of those on the noble path: even the non-returners can expect one more life. Only the seventh of the eight noble individuals, those who have entered the path to arahantship, are assured of enlightenment in this very life. Taken with the previous line, this indicates that those on the path to arahantship first see that the defilements are ending, then (as the next faculty) realize arahantship itself (see [dn34:1.3.25]()). In fact, it would seems as if the point of these three faculties is to clarify this process.
iti62:4.4: The second faculty comes immediately after defilements have ended, when the new arahant reflects on their experience and understands that they are no longer trapped in the cycle of rebirth.
iti62:5.4: The final faculty is the arahant living out their last life in peace.
